newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products hit by U.S. data, gasoline falls.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products hit by U.S. data, gasoline falls.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were lower on bearish U.S. stocks data on Wednesday, with gasoline worst hit, traders said.
Weaker crude and Tuesday's API report for U.S. oil stocks, showing a surprising decline in demand for gasoline, pushed the product into retreat. It sank $2 a tonne, traders said.
However, tight low octane supplies and some demand for product into the East Med were supportive. Prompt Eurograde cargoes valued $2 lower at around $205 a tonne cif Med.
Naphtha was easier and discussion very thin with an industry meeting keeping most players out of the market.
"We had been looking to some extent for increasing gasoline demand to pick this market up," a trader said. Naphtha outright prices were notionally around $1-2 off at $177/$180 a tonne cif.

Eastern demand continued to drive the gas oil market. Traders looking for material to take to India and Singapore were underpinning prices. Italian 0.2 pct was heard on offer for large 45-50kt cargoes at fob high quotes +$5 with bid interest around +$3-3.50 with Russian offered around high fob quotes +$4.
Smaller cargoes not suited for arbitraging were $2 or so cheaper. Cif cargoes were less attractive than fob at around high cif quotes +$3 basis Genoa, traders said.
Diesel was quiet with prices held at high fob EN590 quotes +$2-3, although a large 58kt parcel is destined eastwards.
High sulphur prices held steady but were set to fall as soon as good cargo supply becomes prompt, traders said.
"There is no buying, or at least very little buying," one trader said. Offers were heard around $79 fob with barrels showing out of Greece, France, Syria, Spain, Italy and from trade stock.
